answers.text: Diffusion is particles spreading from where there are lots of them to where there are fewer, down a concentration gradient. Osmosis is the same idea but for water moving through a partially permeable membrane, from high water potential to low water potential.

(a) The substrate enters the active site and the enzyme moulds itself around it rather than being a rigid lock. Holding the substrate in exactly the right position makes the reaction much more likely, and afterwards the products leave and the enzyme can be used again. (b) Heat breaks the weak bonds that hold the enzyme in shape. The active site changes shape so the substrate cannot bind any more, which is denaturation, and the rate of reaction drops.
Animal cells have no cell wall while plant cells are surrounded by one. Plant cells have a large permanent vacuole; animal cells only have small vacuoles if any.

Without a nucleus there is extra space inside the cell for haemoglobin, meaning more oxygen can be transported. The biconcave shape also gives a large surface area and lets the cell deform through narrow capillaries.
